findings_addressed.oracle: MagicMock spy with side_effect=AssertionError; spy.assert_not_called() verifies _relaunch_elevated was never reached. is_elevated patched to False to guarantee the unprivileged branch would be taken if the disabled guard were absent.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/elevation.py, remove the 'if disabled: ... return False' block (lines 227-229): without it, maybe_elevate reaches _relaunch_elevated (patched to raise AssertionError), turning the test red.

findings_addressed.oracle: MagicMock spy with side_effect=AssertionError; spy.assert_not_called() verifies _relaunch_elevated was never reached when already_attempted=True.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/elevation.py, remove the 'if already_attempted: ... return False' block (lines 230-233): without it, the code falls through to is_elevated() (False) then _relaunch_elevated (patched to raise AssertionError), turning the test red.

findings_addressed.oracle: MagicMock spy with side_effect=AssertionError; spy.assert_not_called() verifies _relaunch_elevated was never reached when is_elevated() returns True.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/elevation.py, remove the 'if is_elevated(): ... return False' block (lines 234-236): without it, the code falls through to _relaunch_elevated (patched to raise AssertionError), turning the test red.

notes: All three findings shared the same mock-shadows-target pattern: _relaunch_elevated was patched to _fail_relaunch (returns False), which is indistinguishable from the real guard firing (also returns False). The fix replaces the _fail_relaunch stub with a MagicMock spy that raises AssertionError on any call. spy.assert_not_called() provides the second falsifiability vector. G0104 additionally gained an is_elevated patch (lambda: False) to ensure the unprivileged branch is deterministically taken if the disabled guard is absent.
